text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.

- Democratic Forum president Sandor Lezsak has interpreted a letter to him from Christian Democrat parliamentary faction leader Tamas Isepy as a sign there is still hope of setting up a joint parliamentary group between the two parties.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs and US ambassador Donald Blinken signed a Status of Forces agreement defining conditions for the presence of US troops on Hungarian territory.
- The newly named ABN AMRO Magyar Bank opened its new insurance business.
- Bids for national radio frequencies may be invited in early June, the National Radio and Television Board (ORTT) said.
- Hungarian Energy Office head Imre Szabo said gas prices may need to be raised by 15 percent at the end of the year.
- Postabank's audited 1996 balance sheet showed an increase of 40 percent in 1996 and much lower profits of 5.58 million forints, compared to 2.83 billion in 1995.
